# Rules Logic Checklist: Rules for Form Connections, with Groups and Branches

**Purpose**: Test the quality of spec.md's requirements for branch propagation, rule evaluation and
its delivery to serviceBW, and live changes and data safety, before `/speckit-tasks`
**Created**: 2026-10-24
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)
**Scope**: spec.md only, including whether its body agrees with its Clarifications. The rules
step's UX and accessibility are left out; cross-artifact consistency is left to `/speckit-analyze`.

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 - Are upper limits specified for branches per form connection, rules and groups per branch, and the lengths of names, descriptions and error messages, with what happens when one is exceeded? [Gap]
  - Left to the plan: data-model.md, "Validation" and the Branch and Rule tables (at most 20 branches and 200 items per branch; names of 1–100 characters, descriptions and messages up to 500).
- [x] CHK002 - Is the main branch's default name specified, for new form connections and for those that FR-018 migrates? [Gap, Spec §FR-018, §FR-020]
  - Spec updated: FR-018 ("Standard").
- [x] CHK003 - Does the spec define the order of rules and groups within a level, whether a team member can change it, and where a rule that the main branch adds appears in a based branch that added or grouped rules of its own? [Gap, Spec §FR-021, §FR-022]
  - Spec updated: FR-007 (order kept, no reordering), FR-021 (where the main branch's additions appear), Assumptions "Out of scope", Clarifications (requirements checklist).
- [x] CHK004 - Is it defined what a sub-group becomes when its group is dissolved and it moves to the top level: a group, keeping its identifier, name ("Sub-group 04") and message? [Gap, Spec §FR-008, §FR-010]
  - Spec updated: FR-008 (it becomes a group and keeps its identifier, name, AND or OR, and message).
- [x] CHK005 - Does the spec state whether a deleted branch's identifier can ever be given to a later branch, so that the deleted branch's pull URL keeps answering "unavailable"? [Gap, Spec §FR-025, §FR-027]
  - Spec updated: FR-025 (never reused), FR-027 ("unavailable" for good).
- [x] CHK006 - Is the shape of the evaluation specified, or explicitly delegated to the integration contract: how each outcome and message is tied to its identifier, whether names are included, and what the answer carries instead for requests that aren't completed? [Gap, Spec §FR-010]
  - Left to the plan: contracts/integration-api.md, "evaluation" (results and messages with identifiers, names for display only, `null` without documents).
- [x] CHK007 - Is the order of the reported error messages specified, and whether identical messages of several unmet rules are reported once or once per rule? [Gap, Spec §FR-011]
  - Left to the plan: research R7 and contracts/integration-api.md (the rules step's order, now fixed by FR-007; one message per rule or group, each with its identifier).
- [x] CHK008 - Is the behaviour specified when the evaluation fails unexpectedly during a pull: are the documents delivered with or without an evaluation, or does the pull fail, and can the documents still be obtained afterwards, given they're handed over only once? [Gap, Exception Flow, Spec §FR-015, §FR-017]
  - Spec updated: FR-017, Edge Cases "The evaluation fails".
- [x] CHK009 - Is it explicit that spec 001's network restriction (FR-017) and encryption (FR-019) cover every branch's pull URL, beyond the general "every requirement of spec 001 still applies"? [Gap, Spec §FR-025, §Assumptions]
  - Already covered: spec 001's FR-017 and FR-019 speak of all pull URLs, and Assumptions "Builds on spec 001" keeps them. Plan: research R3 (nginx allow-list, access-log redaction).

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK010 - Is it enumerated which edits make an inherited rule or group "changed" in a branch: condition, value, letter-case choice, error message, name, AND or OR, and in particular its position or group membership? [Clarity, Spec §FR-022, §FR-023]
  - Spec updated: FR-022 (what counts as a change); moves in FR-021, grouping in FR-022.
- [x] CHK011 - Is it defined whether an inherited rule edited back to exactly the main branch's version stays "changed", or follows the main branch again without an undo? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-022, §FR-024]
  - Spec updated: FR-024 (follows again after an edit in the branch, not after a change in the main branch), Clarifications.
- [x] CHK012 - Is it defined whether removing a group also removes the rules in it, as FR-024's undo implies for a branch, and whether ungrouping without removing is an operation of its own, with how each propagates to based branches? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-021, §FR-024]
  - Spec updated: FR-008 (ungroup, delete with members; inherited groups in a branch are only removed), User Story 2 scenario 8, Clarifications.
- [x] CHK013 - Is it specified whether the main branch moving a rule into or out of a group also moves it in a based branch that changed that rule, given FR-022 rules this out only for groups the branch formed itself? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-021, §FR-022]
  - Spec updated: FR-021 (moves are followed, changed items included).
- [x] CHK014 - Is the moment a branch deletion takes effect unambiguous: on confirming it, as User Story 3's scenario 9 reads, or on saving, as FR-028 implies? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-027, §FR-028, §User Story 3]
  - Spec updated: FR-020, FR-027, User Story 3 scenario 9 (on saving).
- [x] CHK015 - Is name uniqueness, for branches and for rules and groups within a branch, defined as respecting or ignoring letter case and spaces at the start and end? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, §FR-020]
  - Spec updated: FR-005, FR-020 (ignoring both).
- [x] CHK016 - Is the identifier scheme fully specified: one sequence shared by rules, groups and sub-groups or one per kind (as "Rule 07" and "Group 03" might suggest), and when an identifier counts as used (on creation in the editor or on the first save), so that "never reused" has a testable meaning across abandoned edits, failed saves and concurrent edits? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, §FR-010]
  - Left to the plan: research R5 (`rule-{n}` and `group-{n}` from two counters; numbered in the editor, fixed on save, shifted under concurrent saves; counters never lowered).
- [x] CHK017 - Does the spec define which items count for a branch's evaluation and its per-item results (sub-groups included, items marked removed and groups dissolved in the branch excluded), and whether a based branch whose rules are all removed counts as "a branch without rules"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009, §FR-010, §FR-023]
  - Spec updated: FR-009, FR-010.
- [x] CHK018 - Is it explicit that every rule and group that counts is evaluated and reported, even when another item has already decided its level's outcome? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009, §FR-010]
  - Left to the plan: contracts/integration-api.md, `results` lists every evaluated rule and group.
- [x] CHK019 - Is it specified which message is reported for a rule that couldn't be checked: its error message, or a distinct one? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011, §FR-014]
  - Already decided: one message per rule (Assumptions, "Error messages"); the outcome `not_checked` lets serviceBW tell the cases apart (FR-014, contracts/integration-api.md).
- [x] CHK020 - Is "the moment the citizen shared their documents" tied to an observable event, such as approval in the wallet (spec 001, SC-004) or the middleware receiving the documents, so that the reference date can be determined around midnight? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012]
  - Left to the plan: research R7 (the request's completion, EUDIPLO's `consumedAt`, as a calendar date in Europe/Berlin).
- [x] CHK021 - Are "is before" and "is after" a given date specified as strict, excluding the date itself, as the number conditions are? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003]
  - Spec updated: FR-003, Dates.
- [x] CHK022 - Is an empty value told apart from a missing one: is an empty text, or a licence with no classes, "couldn't be checked" or evaluated (so that "includes none of B" is met)? And is an empty or spaces-only value in a rule incomplete under FR-006? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-006, §FR-013, §FR-014]
  - Spec updated: FR-014 (empty counts as missing), FR-006 (an empty text value leaves the condition incomplete).
- [x] CHK023 - Is it specified how enum conditions treat a document value outside the field's fixed set, such as an unknown licence class code or a country code in another form: compared as is, or "couldn't be checked"? [Gap, Spec §FR-003, §FR-014]
  - Spec updated: FR-003, Enums.
- [x] CHK024 - Is it specified whether a class that the licence lists but whose own expiry date has passed counts as held, for "Licence classes includes one of" and for FR-014's exception for classes the licence doesn't hold? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-003, §FR-014]
  - Spec updated: FR-003, fields made of parts.
- [x] CHK025 - Do the text comparison rules address Unicode normalisation (a composed "ö" against a decomposed one) and repeated spaces inside a value, beyond letter case and spaces at the start and end? [Gap, Spec §FR-013]
  - Spec updated: FR-013. Plan: research R7 (NFC).

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK026 - Does FR-010's "one added in a branch gets a new identifier" conflict with FR-022's branch version that "counts as added" once the main branch removes the original: does that version keep the main branch's identifier? [Conflict, Spec §FR-010, §FR-022]
  - Spec updated: FR-010, Edge Cases "The main branch removes a rule that a branch changed" (it keeps its identifier).
- [x] CHK027 - Are FR-008 and FR-022 consistent when the main branch's removal leaves a group that a branch changed (for example switched to OR) with one rule: is it dissolved, discarding a change that FR-022 says MUST NOT be discarded? [Conflict, Spec §FR-008, §FR-022]
  - Spec updated: FR-022 (the one exception, named in the main branch's confirmation), Edge Cases "The main branch leaves a group that a branch changed with one rule", SC-006, Clarifications.
- [x] CHK028 - Is it specified whether rules marked removed in a branch count for the checks on deselected fields, and, if they do, how such a rule is cleared, since FR-024 forbids changing or deleting it there? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-006, §FR-024, §FR-029]
  - Spec updated: FR-006 (they're checked, and cleared through the main branch, which they mirror).
- [x] CHK029 - Is "the later save wins" reconciled with SC-006's "0 of the changes made in those branches are lost", and is its granularity defined for rules and branches (whole rule set, branch or rule), given spec 001 applies it to "anything both of them changed"? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases, §SC-006]
  - Spec updated: FR-028 (warn, then reload or replace; the rules of all branches count as one), Edge Cases "Two team members editing the rules at the same time", SC-006 (propagation only), Clarifications.

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK030 - Is it specified what a based branch shows when the main branch adds a rule to a group that the branch removed outright, or to a group the branch changed? The clarification of 2026-10-23 covers only a group dissolved by removing one of its rules. [Gap, Spec §FR-021, §FR-024, §Clarifications 2026-10-23]
  - Spec updated: FR-021.
- [x] CHK031 - Are name clashes covered where no name is entered: a rule the main branch adds with its default name, a copy or duplicate, or an undo that restores the main branch's name, when the branch already uses that name for another rule? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-005, §FR-022, §FR-024]
  - Spec updated: FR-005 (default names kept for their number; names an undo or restore could bring back count as taken), Clarifications.
- [x] CHK032 - Is it specified what a based branch receives when a rule is copied to the main branch and to that branch at once, or from that branch to the main branch, where the linked copy lands beside the original? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-021, §FR-022]
  - Spec updated: FR-022, copies.
- [x] CHK033 - Are FR-006's refusals defined for inherited items: is an incomplete rule that based branches inherit reported for the main branch only or for each branch, and do items marked removed count? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, §FR-021, §FR-023]
  - Spec updated: FR-006 (reported once, for the main branch; removed rules are checked).
- [x] CHK034 - Is the precedence among pull answers specified where several apply: form connection deactivated or deleted, branch deleted after the trigger (where FR-025's "every branch that existed … MUST answer with the same status and documents" meets FR-027's "unavailable"), branch added after the trigger, branch of another form connection, and unknown or expired reference? [Coverage, Spec §FR-025, §FR-027]
  - Left to the plan: research R3 and contracts/integration-api.md, "Order of the checks" (a deleted branch answers "unavailable" before "existed at the trigger" is considered).
- [x] CHK035 - Is it explicit that spec 001's 60-second repeat window starts with the first pull through any branch and is shared by all branches, and that every repeat evaluates with the same reference date, also across midnight? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012, §FR-017, §Edge Cases]
  - Left to the plan: research R3 (delivery state per request, shared by all branches), R8 (the day of sharing is fixed, so repeats evaluate the same); contracts/integration-api.md, "Which branch serviceBW pulls".
- [x] CHK036 - Is the evaluation specified for a request triggered before the feature was deployed and pulled after it, which has no rules from its trigger time? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-018, §FR-028, §SC-005]
  - Left to the plan: research R8, R11 (requests without a rule set are evaluated as met).

- [x] CHK038 - Is the migration of existing form connections required to happen completely or not at all, so that none is left without a main branch or with a changed pull URL? [Coverage, Recovery, Spec §FR-018, §SC-005]

- [x] CHK039 - Does FR-017's ban on logging the evaluation extend to anything that reveals a citizen's outcome, such as a failure report naming the rule being evaluated or the value it couldn't interpret? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
- Focus: branches and propagation (FR-008, FR-018 to FR-024), evaluation and serviceBW (FR-009 to
  FR-017, FR-025 to FR-027), live changes and data safety (FR-017, FR-028, FR-029). Depth: standard
  gate before `/speckit-tasks`, for the author or a PR reviewer
- Some items may already be answered in research.md, data-model.md or the contracts (for example
  server limits, the pull check order and the evaluation's shape). Such an item is still a gap in
  spec.md: either the spec takes the decision over, or the reviewer accepts the delegation and
  notes where it lives
- Review of 2026-10-24: the reviewer accepted the plan's decisions for the items noted "Left to the
  plan" or "Already covered", and decided the rest, which spec.md now records ("Spec updated")
- 2026-10-25: the reviewer accepted the spec edits, and every item is marked `[x]`
